subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a pixel-art koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand using the pixel kit's box and texture primitives, aiming for a few hundred parts while keeping the API usage correct and the code manageable in scope.

For the pose, I'm deciding to build a skeleton with named joints, a vertical trunk mounted on a wooden base slab, and have the koala's front face visible to the viewer with arms wrapping around the sides of the trunk to grip it, since that reads as the most natural "koala hugging a tree" silhouette.

Now I'm working out the actual proportions: roughly real-world koala scale (~0.5-0.7m sitting height), a base slab around 0.6x0.06x0.6, and a trunk swept vertically to about 1.25m with a tapering radius, plus a sloped branch stub around y=0.38 for the koala to sit on.

I'm positioning the koala's body against the trunk so it reads as clinging/leaning rather than floating, then planning to build it from boxes with pixel-style fur using small textured cells, dithered gray fur with a white chest patch.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton hierarchy: a root joint at the base, branching into hips, spine segments, neck, head and jaw, ears, two arm chains with shoulder-elbow-wrist-finger joints for gripping, and two leg chains with hip-knee-ankle-toe joints, skipping a tail since koalas are tailless.

For the blocky pixel-art limbs, I'm planning a `blockLimb` helper that uses frustum boxes stretched between joints, with small cube blocks placed at bend points to cover any gaps at the joints.

Then I'm working out the chain structure for arms using three points (shoulder, elbow, wrist) so the tip joint lands naturally at the wrist, with role "arm" assigned. For the hands, since koalas have opposable digits meant for gripping, I'll simplify by giving each finger a short two-point chain tagged with role "digit".

Working out the finger placement so hands wrap around the trunk's curved surface, with wrist, mid-finger, and tip points curving from the front toward the back at a slightly larger radius than the trunk itself.

I'll add dark claw tips and a simple palm box near the wrist angle. For the legs, I'm thinking about hip and knee placement so the koala sits gripping the trunk rather than resting on a separate branch stub.

I'm positioning the branch stub so the koala's rump rests on top of it, working out the vertical offset so the body sits naturally at the fork. Now I'm blocking out the torso as stacked boxes—a wider pelvis section and a narrower belly section above it—to get that pear-shaped koala silhouette.

Still shaping the ears...

For the face, I'm planning a black oval nose box mounted near the top-front of the head, with eyes handled via a small pixel texture or textured plane rather than geometry.

I'm leaning toward building the head as a textured skinBox sized around 13×10×10 pixels at a 0.02 texel scale, painting the fur shading, muzzle, chin, and facial features directly onto the texture sheet, while keeping the nose as a separate protruding dark box with a highlight and adding a distinct lower jaw piece.

Working out the exact proportions now: head box roughly 14×9×10 pixels, jaw box about 8×2×7 attached at a joint below it, positioning the head center near y=0.98 so the jaw sits just above the chest top around 0.83-0.89. At texel 0.02 the torso spans about twelve cells, giving a nice chunky pixel-art look for the paint sheet.

I'm figuring out texel density for a 1024px sheet based on total painted surface area (~4m²), landing around 2.3mm per texel so each 0.02 cell covers about 8 texels — solid resolution. Now I'm sketching out color palettes: a gray ramp for the koala's fur, a cream ramp for the belly, and a bark ramp for the trunk, aiming for a eucalyptus ghost-gum look with smooth grey-cream tones.

For the gum trunk I'm using a cream/salmon/green-gray ramp to suggest peeling bark with vertical streak variation per cell, and planning a wood plank tile texture for the base via a procedural pixel texture generator. For the foliage I'm going with cheap textured cards (double-sided, pixel-art eucalyptus leaf shapes) rather than extruded geometry since I need lots of leaves and cards keep things efficient.

Now I'm working out the branch structure: three tapering rod sweeps from the trunk top, with leaf clusters attached using frames sampled along each path. I'm collecting those frames manually from the sweep callback, then feeding them into the cards function with randomized size, lean, and spin so the leaves orient outward and droop naturally along a downward flow direction.

I'm also planning small brown cylinder gumnuts tucked near the branches, and figuring out bone attachment so each branch sweep parents to the trunk joint rather than the root.

Setting up the skeleton with base and trunk joints positioned along the trunk, then starting to write the actual implementation code importing the builder utilities.

Importing the pixel and glow kits along with noise helpers, then defining constants for the trunk's thickness and coordinate positions before setting up a color-snapping palette helper.

I'm limiting myself to a small set of flat colors for the fur gradients, defining dark-to-light grey shades and cream tones as palette arrays for shading the creature.

Jaggedizing the cream chest boundary with noise, then working out the ear geometry—small tilted cylinders at the head sides with a fluffy inner cap texture and outer fur paint for the back.

Still working out ear tuft placement...

Still planning the head pixel layout...

I'm figuring out the nose placement protruding from the front center, a mouth line below it, and a separate lower jaw box. For the side faces I'm reasoning through which viewer direction corresponds to the model's front when looking from the +x side, to get cheek fur tufts oriented correctly.

Working out jaw box placement relative to the hinge, then figuring the nose geometry—a small dark box with a pixel highlight offset to the top-left, positioning it just in front of the muzzle so it embeds slightly into the face.

Now I'm placing the eyes and nose vertically on the head: eyes sit higher, around pixel row 2-3, while the nose is lower and larger, spanning the muzzle's cream-colored rows, with the eyes positioned symmetrically left-right near pixel columns 3 and 10.

Now I'm planning the body structure using boxes for the pear-shaped koala torso, setting up a spine joint chain from hips through two spine segments, then moving on to build the neck chain next.

Setting up the root and trunk joints with their positions, then deciding to parent the spine chain to the root since the koala is perched on the tree. Now I'm sketching out the arm chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist points.

Computing the wrist position puts it nearly behind the trunk's front surface, which means the hand could end up partially occluded by the body—I need the hands to stay visible at the trunk's sides rather than sinking into it.

Rethinking the proportions: the body is wider than the trunk, so from the front the trunk gets mostly hidden except at the sides where the arms wrap around. I should make the trunk thicker—maybe radius 0.11 near the base tapering to 0.06 near the top—so it reads properly against the body width.

I'm defining the trunk's taper with a radius sweep from 0.125 down to 0.06 along the body's height, using an octagonal cross-section for a faceted pixel look, then calculating the hand-grip position by interpolating the radius at y=0.8 and offsetting outward for the finger center.

Now I'm checking finger placement angles to make sure hands sit correctly relative to the shoulder and body width — noticing hands may be partially hidden behind the shoulder, so I'm narrowing the chest width to around 0.2 to improve visibility and adjusting the arm path from shoulder to elbow accordingly.

Placing hand digits and palm geometry...

Still writing digit geometry...

Now I'm working through leg placement, figuring where the feet grip the trunk and computing hip-to-knee-to-ankle positions and bone lengths to make the koala's lower leg proportions look right.

I need the branch to actually support the pelvis, so I'm checking clearances: raising the branch endpoint from (0,0.34,-0.14) to (0,0.42,0.2) closes the 0.04 gap so the branch top meets the pelvis bottom. The legs hang over the sides with enough clearance from the branch radius, and the thighs rest on top as intended.

Now I'm working out torso proportions — pelvis, belly, and chest box dimensions tapering from 0.26 down to 0.2 in width, keeping depth around 0.22, with the chest top meeting the neck/head joint around y 0.88-0.89, and sizing everything in clean 0.02 increments to match the grid.

I'm finding the jaw and chest still overlap, so I'm shifting the head up slightly, recentering it around y 1.02 so the jaw sits just above the chest's upper boundary without intersecting.

Then I'm reworking the chest height down to 0.12 and recalculating torso segment heights so they sum correctly to a top at y 0.90, keeping the shoulder fixed at y 0.82.

Now I'm placing the nose and eyes by computing row positions within the head's vertical span, working out where rows two and three fall to center the eyes correctly.

For the nose, I'm figuring its depth and width relative to the muzzle front, settling on a fairly large box since koalas have prominent noses, and then placing the mouth as a dark line just below it with a short vertical philtrum mark.

Now I'm working out the smile line along the jaw seam and positioning the ears — large round shapes sitting on top of the head's sides, angled slightly outward with octagonal cylinder geometry for the ear outline.

Still writing ear tuft code...

Now I'm planning the pixel textures needed: the head skin sheet, a plank tile for the base, leaf textures, and a small plaque on the base's front face featuring a leaf icon instead of text, keeping it simple as a 16x8 pixel design.

I'm also thinking about adding fur fringe details — small fur-colored boxes scattered around the shoulders and cheeks to give texture, using a surface scatter approach with minimum distance spacing to place around 60 nubs across the torso parts.

Scattering fur limited to front/side normals. Now I'm planning the eucalyptus tree: trunk sweeps from near the base up to 1.4 with a slight sway via catmull points, positioned above the koala's head, and I'm sketching branch placements coming off the upper trunk.

I'm adding a couple more branches, including a small branchlet near the branch the koala sits on so it can have leaves for chewing at the tip.

For the actual sweep geometry, I'm using catmull-spline paths with tapering radii, barkPaint reused from the trunk, and 6-sided section circles for the branches. Then I'm generating leaf placement frames along each branch sweep, picking orientation angles so leaves emerge mostly from the upward-facing side.

Leaves get a random spin around their facing axis so they stay generally upward while fanning outward using a golden-angle-like rotation per leaf index, flattening the flow direction onto the horizontal plane near branch tips so they radiate outward and droop downward like real eucalyptus foliage.

Still writing leaf frame logic...

Generating leaf sprite pixels...

I'm adding a second, warmer leaf texture ramp for variation (new-growth pinkish tones) alongside the main eucalyptus palette, plus small cylindrical gumnut clusters near branches. For the base, I'm building a two-tier wooden plinth with tiled planks, a smaller darker upper box, and brass corner studs.

Working out the plank texel scaling for the base top face...

I'm working out the base colors and structural details—white tint for textured parts, trunk and root positioning, and deciding to skip extras like glowing elements or a joey to keep things simple. For the character's paint, I'm planning fur coloring on torso, arms, and legs with a cream patch on the chest.

I'm also figuring out darker tones for hands, feet, and paw pads versus lighter cream claws for contrast, a dark nose with a subtle highlight, and cream fluff around the chin and jaw. For the torso I'm defining the cream belly patch based on surface normal direction facing forward.

Writing body paint logic...

Filling pixel data...

Still adding facial features...

Actually I'll skip the dark mouth line idea and keep the jaw front cream with slight shading instead, adding just a thin dark seam row at cols 1..6 to suggest the mouth under the head. Then I'm computing the skinBox scale factors so the head's front and side faces map to the right physical dimensions, and assembling the head part from the sheet.

Now I'm placing the jaw box with its size and position so it spans correctly below the head, then defining the jaw joint's pivot and aim direction, followed by the neck and head joints with their own positions and aim targets to build out the sitting koala's skeleton.

Since I'm using absolute coordinates with bone and position references, local frames don't matter here. I'm setting up ear joints parented to the head, then laying out the spine chain (hips, spine1, spine2) with three named points and a "spine" role, before moving on to defining the arm chain's parent joint.

I'll skip adding a tail stub and instead build a helper function for limb boxes using tapered frustum shapes between joints, with small cube pieces at the elbow and slightly varying widths for shoulder versus forearm sections. Writing hand block geometry...

Still placing trunk and wrist points...

Writing taper function...

Working out the koala's leg joint positions from ankle to knee to hip, making sure the thigh and knee boxes have reasonable widths and that the legs drape naturally over the branch. Then I'm shifting to the plant stand's base structure and trunk root flare geometry.

Now I'm sketching out a pixel-art plaque texture generator, defining brass-colored border pixels, a leaf icon stamp pattern, and dash marks to simulate text.

Working out the plaque sizing — I need to scale the pixel glyphs down to a small physical size (around 0.12 x 0.045) so it fits on the base without overwhelming it, since a full 0.09 height is too tall for the base tier.

I'll position the plaque slightly forward of the base's front face so it reads as an overlay, then consider adding a second smaller tier beneath the trunk to give the base a stepped plinth look, adjusting the trunk's starting height accordingly.

For eucalyptus bark, I'm defining a color ramp from mossy greens to tan and salmon, then using stretched noise sampling (vertically elongated to mimic bark streaks) to paint patches—higher noise values trigger salmon-colored patches against the base trunk tones.

I'm adding subtle shading via side-lighting, plus rare dark knots and scars scattered sparsely across the surface. I'm also planning droopy foliage frames and leaves hanging near the koala's reach, along with tiny gum blossom buds, though I may simplify or skip those details.

Now I'm tallying the total part count across all elements—torso, fur nubs, head, ears with tufts, arms, legs, trunk, branches, base, leaves, and gumnuts—landing around 170 parts total, which feels like a reasonable budget, so I'm considering adding more fur nubs for density.

Setting up imports...
